$comment: Company data fields (founder 2026-10-07; spec pages + identifier widening 2026-10-08): the typed company-level data values the repo genuinely consumes. Honest derivation rule, widened once and deliberately for the identifier fields: a field exists here only because a committed processes/artifacts.json artifact establishes it (producedBy) AND one of two committed consumption paths is real - (a) a committed lib/openstartup exported function takes it (signatures read from the module source; consumedBy names the real exported function and the parameter/property the value enters as), OR (b) a committed corpus process requires-and-carries it: the establishing artifact sits in the requires list of committed processes/corpus.json records, which consume the value through the artifact (the EIN entered on the bank KYC and payroll setup, the Delaware file number the annual-report portal keys on). Path-(b) fields carry no consumedBy; their consuming processes are computed from the corpus requires edges, never hand-listed. Never speculative either way. Each field also carries its spec (founder 2026-10-08): format sentence, regex pattern where the authority's format is strict, the authority's own documented example where one exists (never an invented number), the assigning/defining authority, the documents the value appears on, and URL citations for the format claims (every URL fetch-verified when curated). Totality is tested in lib/__tests__/companyFields.test.ts; read back by lib/companyFields.ts; rendered on /fields and /fields/[id], on /artifacts/[id] (Data fields this artifact establishes) and /open-modules/[id] (fields the module consumes). Schema: schemas/company-fields.schema.json.

fields.label: Date of incorporation
fields.description: The date the company legally comes into existence - the start of the recurring compliance clock (DE franchise tax, Form 1120, payroll quarters).

spec.format: A calendar date; the open modules consume it as an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (the committed wire contract in lib/openstartup/deadlines.ts).
spec.authority: Fixed by the Delaware Division of Corporations filing: corporate existence commences when the certificate is filed (DGCL section 106).
whereItAppears: The Delaware annual franchise tax report

sources.label: Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Chapter 1, Subchapter I (formation; section 102 certificate contents, section 106 commencement of corporate existence)

fields.label: Fiscal year end
fields.description: The company's tax-year end - declared on the SS-4 when the EIN is obtained (calendar-year December 31 for most startups); it positions the federal return deadline.

spec.format: A calendar date; the open modules consume it as an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (the committed wire contract in lib/openstartup/deadlines.ts).
spec.authority: Declared by the company to the IRS: Form SS-4 line 12 asks for the closing month of the accounting year, and the Form 1120 return covers that tax year.
whereItAppears: Form SS-4 line 12 (closing month of accounting year)
The Form 1120 header (the tax year the return covers)

sources.label: IRS Instructions for Form SS-4
IRS Instructions for Form 1120

fields.label: Founder stock transfer date
fields.description: The date the restricted founder stock is transferred - the event the 30-day 83(b) election window runs from.

spec.format: A calendar date; the open modules consume it as an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (the committed wire contract in lib/openstartup/deadlines.ts).
spec.authority: Fixed by the restricted stock purchase: the date the property is transferred, as the 83(b) election form reports it (Form 15620 box 3).
whereItAppears: The founder restricted stock purchase agreement
Form 15620 box 3 (the date the property is transferred)

sources.label: IRS Form 15620, Section 83(b) Election

fields.label: Authorized shares
fields.description: Total shares the charter authorizes - the driver of Delaware's authorized-shares franchise-tax method and one side of the method comparison.

spec.format: A positive whole-number share count, stated per class in the charter.
spec.authority: Stated in the Certificate of Incorporation under DGCL section 102(a)(4); the Division of Corporations taxes on it under the authorized-shares method.
whereItAppears: The Certificate of Incorporation (authorized classes and counts)
The Delaware annual franchise tax report

sources.label: Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Chapter 1, Subchapter I (formation; section 102 certificate contents, section 106 commencement of corporate existence)
Delaware Division of Corporations, How To Calculate Franchise Taxes

fields.label: Par value per share
fields.description: The charter's par value per authorized share class - an input of the assumed-par-value-capital franchise-tax method.

spec.format: A USD amount per share, commonly a small fraction of a cent, stated per authorized class.
spec.authority: Stated in the Certificate of Incorporation under DGCL section 102(a)(4); the assumed-par-value-capital method computes from it.
whereItAppears: The Delaware annual franchise tax report (assumed-par method)

sources.label: Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Chapter 1, Subchapter I (formation; section 102 certificate contents, section 106 commencement of corporate existence)
Delaware Division of Corporations, How To Calculate Franchise Taxes

fields.label: Issued shares
fields.description: Total shares actually issued across all classes - the cap table's bottom line and the denominator of Delaware's assumed-par method.

spec.format: A whole-number share count totaled across all classes actually issued.
spec.authority: Set by board-authorized issuances recorded on the cap table; reported to Delaware as total issued shares on the annual franchise tax report.
whereItAppears: The Delaware annual franchise tax report (issued shares, assumed-par method)

sources.label: Delaware Division of Corporations, How To Calculate Franchise Taxes

fields.label: Total gross assets
fields.description: The Form 1120 Schedule L total-asset figure - the assumed-par franchise-tax method's asset input and the QSBS $50M gross-asset condition's fact.

spec.format: A USD amount: the total assets figure as reported on Form 1120 Schedule L.
spec.authority: Delaware defines the assumed-par method input as the "total assets" reported on U.S. Form 1120, Schedule L; the QSBS condition reads aggregate gross assets under IRC section 1202(d).
whereItAppears: The Delaware annual franchise tax report (assumed-par method)

sources.label: Delaware Division of Corporations, How To Calculate Franchise Taxes
26 U.S.C. section 1202 (qualified small business stock; the aggregate-gross-assets condition)

fields.label: Fully diluted shares
fields.description: Issued + options + pool + as-converted instruments - the denominator every ownership percentage and pool-sizing computation divides by.

spec.format: A whole-number share count: issued shares plus outstanding options, the unissued pool, and as-converted instruments.
spec.authority: Cap-table convention; the committed reference definition is the YC post-money SAFE's company capitalization (fully-diluted basis).

sources.label: Y Combinator, SAFE documents (the post-money SAFE user guide defines company capitalization on a fully-diluted basis)
The Holloway Guide to Equity Compensation

fields.label: Unissued option pool
fields.description: Pool shares reserved but not yet granted - what the pool-increase computations top up to hit a target available percentage.

spec.format: A whole-number share count: shares reserved under the equity incentive plan but not yet granted.
spec.authority: Set by the equity incentive plan's board- and stockholder-approved share reserve, tracked on the cap table.
whereItAppears: The equity incentive plan share reserve

sources.label: The Holloway Guide to Equity Compensation

fields.label: Cash on hand
fields.description: Cash in the business bank account now - the numerator of every runway computation.

spec.format: A USD amount read from the business bank account.
spec.authority: The company's bank records; the runway arithmetic it feeds follows Paul Graham's default-alive framing.

sources.label: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead? (October 2015)

fields.label: Monthly revenue
fields.description: Current monthly revenue run rate from the books - one side of net burn in the default-alive projection.

spec.format: A USD amount per month, read from the books as the current run rate.
spec.authority: The company's accounting ledger; one side of net burn in the default-alive projection.

sources.label: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead? (October 2015)

fields.label: Monthly operating expenses
fields.description: Gross burn - current monthly operating expenses from the books, the other side of net burn.

spec.format: A USD amount per month: current gross operating expenses from the books.
spec.authority: The company's accounting ledger; the other side of net burn in the default-alive projection.

sources.label: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead? (October 2015)

fields.label: Revenue growth (% MoM)
fields.description: Month-over-month revenue growth in percent, measured from the books - what separates default-alive from default-dead.

spec.format: A percent value per month, computed from the books' consecutive monthly revenue figures.
spec.authority: The company's accounting ledger; the growth input of Paul Graham's default-alive versus default-dead test.

sources.label: Paul Graham, Default Alive or Default Dead? (October 2015)

fields.label: Common share FMV (409A)
fields.description: The 409A report's fair market value per common share - the strike-price floor every option grant is sanity-checked against.

spec.format: A USD amount per common share.
spec.authority: Set by the company's 409A valuation under the Treas. Reg. section 1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B) valuation presumptions (independent appraisal for illiquid startups).
whereItAppears: Board consents approving option grants (exercise price at or above FMV)

sources.label: Internal Revenue Bulletin 2007-19, final regulations under section 409A

fields.label: 409A valuation date
fields.description: The as-of date of the current 409A valuation - what the 12-month staleness and refresh-trigger checks run from.

spec.format: A calendar date; the open modules consume it as an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string (the committed wire contract in lib/openstartup/deadlines.ts).
spec.authority: The as-of date of the 409A valuation report; the independent-appraisal presumption holds for no more than 12 months absent a material change (Treas. Reg. section 1.409A-1(b)(5)(iv)(B)).

sources.label: Internal Revenue Bulletin 2007-19, final regulations under section 409A

fields.label: Runs payroll
fields.description: Whether the company runs payroll - established by the payroll account existing; it switches the Form 941 quarterlies into the compliance calendar.

spec.format: yes or no: whether a payroll account exists and the company pays wages.
spec.authority: Follows from paying wages: employers who pay wages subject to withholding file Form 941 quarterly (IRS).

sources.label: IRS Instructions for Form 941

fields.label: Employer Identification Number (EIN)
fields.description: The federal tax identification number itself, assigned by the IRS when the SS-4 application is approved. Consumed through the EIN artifact: the committed corpus requires it to open the bank account, register state taxes, set up payroll, connect a payment processor, get insurance quotes, and file the federal return.

spec.format: Nine digits arranged as two digits, a hyphen, then seven digits (00-0000000).
whereItAppears: The IRS CP 575 EIN confirmation letter
Bank account and payment processor KYC

sources.label: IRS Instructions for Form SS-4: "An EIN is a 9-digit number (for example, 12-3456789)"
IRS Publication 15 (Employer's Tax Guide): "The EIN is a nine-digit number the IRS issues. The digits are arranged as follows: 00-0000000."

fields.label: State file number
fields.description: The Business Entity File Number the Delaware Division of Corporations assigns when the formation filing is accepted. Consumed through the charter artifact the committed corpus requires: the annual report and franchise tax filing keys on it, and state registrations copy it.

spec.format: A numeric file number of up to 9 digits, assigned by the Delaware Division of Corporations.
whereItAppears: The Delaware filing cover of the stamped Certificate of Incorporation
The eCorp annual report and franchise tax filing (the portal keys on the file number)
The Division of Corporations entity search

sources.label: Delaware Division of Corporations eCorp File Number Entry: "Please enter your Business Entity File Number below to start filing your Annual Report or Pay Taxes"; "The File Number can be up to 9 digits in length"
Delaware Division of Corporations, Annual Report and Tax Instructions
